title: What’s in a name?
html_source: Juliet asks this question in Romeo and Juliet, Act II, Scene 2.

anchor.prefix: m, as dear as the coat of arms he toadied for, on a bend sable a spear or steeled argent, honorificabilitudinitatibus, dearer than his glory of greatest shakescene in the country.
anchor.suffix: That is what we ask ourselves in childhood when we write the name that we are told is ours. A star, a daystar, a firedrake, rose at his birth. It shone by day in the heavens alone
